title: test(plugin-auth): the forced-reset OAuth test takes its token time from the routine reset, not the wall clock
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8XGffEBTNhotjbfjKWmvMXT)_

Fixes #36361

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感，只改一条登录插件的测试；产品行为不变。
- 为什么做：这条测试在合并队列满载时会偶发变红，把无关的 PR 踢出队列，堵住主干。
- 出错会怎样：只影响测试本身，产品代码一行未动，可直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

One test, `an administrator's forced reset ends them too and reports the apps; with revocation off it ends none`
in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts`. Test-only: no product file moves.

The test used to take its token's `iat` as `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 1` **before** the routine admin reset ran.
Now it runs the routine reset first, reads the credential-change time that reset wrote
(`readCredentialChangedAt`, the same reader the MCP door uses), and takes `iat` as the first whole second at or
after it (`Math.ceil(changedAtMs / 1000)`). The forced-reset half is unchanged.

The slow call is pinned: just before the routine reset the test moves the wall clock two seconds on
(`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })` + `vi.setSystemTime`, the same pattern the file's credential-change
describe already uses), standing in for an admin call that takes longer than a second under load. Every run now
takes the path the queue build failed on. The describe's `afterEach` restores real timers.

## Why — root cause is the test's clock, not the product

`mcpConsentAdmits` places a token with no millisecond claim on a consent row at `iat * 1000` and refuses it when that
is earlier than the account's credential-change time (`issuedBeforeCredentialChange`). The routine reset
(`revokeSessionsAndKeys: false`) writes a new change time. The old test fixed `iat` at most one second ahead of the
clock it read *before* the reset, so it assumed the admin HTTP call finished inside that second. Under full-suite
load the call took longer, the change time landed after `iat * 1000`, and the door correctly refused a token that,
by its own `iat`, predates the reset: `expected false to be true` at line 538 (merge-queue run 44999732595, Test
Core 10/10). The product rule is right; the test's premise about timing was wrong.

The two other `+ 1` sites in the file (the self-service reset case at line 468, the disabled-app case at line 983)
have no credential change between taking `iat` and the assertion that needs it to stand, so they cannot hit this.

## Tests

All on head `b4de067d`.

- **The pin fails without the fix.** `main`'s version of the test with only the two clock lines added fails at the
  card's assertion: `AssertionError: expected false to be true` at the `grantStands()` right after the routine reset
  (the same line as merge-queue run 44999732595, shifted by the two inserted lines). The fixed test passes in the
  same run. The `main` copy was temporary and is not in the diff.
- Before the pin existed, the same was shown with a real 1.5 s pause in place of the clock move: red on `main`,
  green with the fix.
- The fixed test, 20 consecutive runs: 20/20 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` (including `check:test-typecheck`): passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`: 293 files, 6265 passed, 10 skipped.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the changed file: clean.

No skip, no narrowing, no retry wrapper, no timeout change.

## Acceptance notes

None.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts -t "forced reset ends them too"` — 1 passed. Swap the two `issuedAt` lines back to `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 1` taken before the routine reset and it fails with `expected false to be true`.

Files to read first: in `password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts`, the forced-reset case (the clock move and the `iat` read back), then the describe's `afterEach` (`vi.useRealTimers()`).

Changeset: none; the diff changes a test file only and publishes nothing (`skip-changeset`).
